name: Daniel Metzler
current_role: CEO and Co-Founder, Isar Aerospace SE (Ottobrunn/Munich, Germany)
profile: Austrian-born engineer who co-founded launch company Isar Aerospace in 2018 out of TUM's WARR student rocketry group. Its Spectrum rocket failed ~30s into its March 2025 debut, but on 5 Sept 2026 the second flight reached orbit and deployed payloads; he is now scaling production toward up to 40 vehicles/year.
interesting_fact: On 5 Sept 2026 Isar Aerospace became the first commercial company from continental Europe to deliver satellites to orbit, on only its second flight, from Andøya, Norway (mission 'Onward and Upward').
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Feldkirch, Vorarlberg (Austria), studied mechanical engineering in Vienna, then moved to Munich where he led WARR's ~40-student high-altitude research rocket project. He told VOL.at: 'Es gibt unendlich viel über Raumfahrt zu lernen.'
notes: Frequent conference speaker (SmallSat Europe, DLD, BDI space congress) and podcast guest (Mostly Awesome #18), so a podcast pitch via the press office is a natural route. Co-founder Josef Fleischmann left operations in Sept 2026 to found Bavaria Instruments.

name: Avery Pennarun
profile: Canadian software engineer and Waterloo alum who co-founded Tailscale (WireGuard-based zero-config mesh VPN) in 2019 after stints in fintech and at Google (payments, then Google Fiber's WiFi/platform team). Tailscale raised a $160M Series C led by Accel in April 2025 at a ~$1.5B valuation and is pushing into identity-aware access and AI gateways.
interesting_fact: Tailscale grew to $10M+ ARR largely through bottom-up developer adoption with almost no marketing; the product idea came from a former colleague at a Canadian bank who needed secure server access.
deep_cut_fact: His networking obsession started as a kid fighting his sister over the family modem; by grade 10 he was writing Linux drivers for old network cards, and at university he co-founded Net Integration Technologies (office internet-sharing box, later bought by IBM). He also wrote open-source tools wvdial, sshuttle, bup and redo.
notes: Very accessible public writer (long-running apenwarr.ca blog) and frequent podcast guest (Stratechery interview 2025, Heavybit, Linux Unplugged). A thoughtful-essay angle (e.g. his blog posts on systems design) would land well. Bluesky link is published on his own blog; field type 'x' used for it.

profile: Ubras is a Beijing-based 'size-free' wireless bra/underwear brand founded in 2016, backed by Sequoia China (HongShan) and Capital Today, which outsold Uniqlo in the category on Singles' Day 2020. Public reporting names 钭雅前 (Concon, ex-Aimer marketing director) as founder; a shareholder named 赵莹 (Zhao Ying) reportedly holds ~20% of the operating company. interesting_fact: Ubras popularised 'no-size' (无尺码) wire-free bras in China and in 2020 outsold Uniqlo in underwear during Singles' Day.
notes: Identity uncertain: the founder widely reported is 钭雅前; a 20.28% shareholder named 赵莹 appears in third-party registry data (https://pitchhub.36kr.com/project/1713134360160775), likely this person but unconfirmed. Very low public profile; any approach would go via Ubras corporate channels.
